**Premise correction:** This repository (the `usememos/memos` Go server) does not contain any per-user API rate-limiting middleware, so there is no such component or set of request limits to point to.

What I checked to confirm this:

- Full-text search across `*.go`, `*.ts`, `*.tsx` for `limiter`, `throttle`, `ratelimit`, `requests per`, `rps`, etc. turned up nothing relevant to API request throttling — the only two hits were in `web/src/components/MemoEditor/Editor/formatting.ts` and `listIndent.ts`, which are unrelated editor-formatting code.
- `go.mod`/`go.sum` contain no rate-limiting dependency (e.g. no `golang.org/x/time/rate`, `ulule/limiter`, etc.).
- The server's middleware/interceptor chain is fully enumerated in two places and neither includes rate limiting:
  - Echo-level middleware in `server/server.go` (`50:53:/bench/repo/server/server.go`): only `middleware.Recover()` and a CORS middleware (`newCORSMiddleware`).
  - gRPC-Gateway/Connect middleware in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (`64:147:/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`): a `gatewayAuthMiddleware` for the gRPC-Gateway mux, and for Connect handlers a chain of `NewMetadataInterceptor()`, `NewLoggingInterceptor()`, `NewRecoveryInterceptor()`, and `NewAuthInterceptor()` — again, no limiter.
- The only "limit" mechanisms present are unrelated to per-user API rate limiting: `maxAPIRequestBytes` (a 256 MiB request body cap, line 20 of `v1.go`), and `thumbnailSemaphore` / `imageProcessingSemaphore` (`golang.org/x/sync/semaphore`-based concurrency caps of 3 and 2, restricting simultaneous thumbnail/image processing to prevent memory exhaustion — not per-user, not request-count based).
- `internal/email/doc.go` line 86 mentions "Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse" as a design note/comment, but this isn't implemented as middleware and isn't related to general API requests.

So there is no code path in this repo implementing per-user API rate limiting, and consequently no configured request limits to report.
